Title: Nurturing children for a sustainable tomorrow
NewsSummary: AKU launches programme to promote Early Childhood Development in Arusha, Tanzania
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University's Institute for Educational Development East Africa (IED, EA) and the Institute for Human Development (IHD) have jointly launched a three-year project that seeks to promote the wellbeing of children.  

The project titled "Evidence Based Policy, Planning, and Development - Supporting Children's Holistic Development in Marginalized Communities" was launched in Arusha, Tanzania following a successful launch of the same in Kenya. This project is funded by the Hilton foundation and it will serve the disadvantaged communities in Tanzania and Kenya. 

This programme aims to provide an avenue for caregivers, early childhood development workers, policy makers and practitioners to gain knowledge and insights towards promoting Early Childhood Development, ECD.  

Dr Jane Rarieya, Interim Dean at the Institute for Educational Development, East Africa said, "If we nurture our children well early on, we create a society which is lasting, cohesive, innovative and which will continue to push forward the legacy and the lessons instilled in them from a very young age."

The knowledge generated from this project will inform policy, programs design and implementation. It will also enable the redesigning and adaptation of existing interventions to deliver contextually relevant, evidence-based integrated ECD interventions that enhance maternal and child outcomes that are co-designed and piloted across communities with similar conditions in Tanzania and Kenya. 

" This project will be of great benefit to the people of Arusha as it enables the elimination of child development challenges. The project will also assist in policymaking and legislation as it will be accompanied by research on child development issues," said Mr John Mongella, Regional Commissioner for Arusha.

IHD Director, Prof Amina Abubakar added, "In selecting the work, we want to do with this project, one of the things that we have really focused on is how we can ensure that children in marginalized communities receive quality care. We also want to know how we can train the workforce serving children to have the right skills and expertise and learn from each other's experiences to improve the quality of services that we provide to children." 

The initiative will provide a platform for ECD stakeholders to share their insights and learn from each other through interactive webinars. The public will also have free access to information on best practices they can adopt to promote quality childcare. 

The project includes a longitudinal research study to be conducted in Tanzania and Kenya with Professor Amina Abubakar as the Principal Investigator and lead for Kenya, and Dr Fortidas Bakuza as the Co-Principal Investigator and lead for Tanzania.
